blockingLimits.text: Unlisted commercial apps: conversations.history / replies at 1 request/minute, 15 objects per call, for installs after 2025-05-29. Listing in the Marketplace lifts it.

usageRows.notes: Self-serve to install anywhere, but history reads are throttled until you're in the Slack Marketplace, which means 10 active workspaces and an enhanced review.

verdict.oneLiner: Self-serve to install in any workspace, but unlisted apps can read history only once a minute — production-volume reading needs a Slack Marketplace listing (10 active workspaces, up to ~12 weeks of review).

steps.title: Copy the Composio callback URL
steps.detail: In Composio: Authentication management → Create Auth Config → Slack → OAuth2 → Use your own developer credentials. The redirect URI is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

steps.title: Create a Slack app
steps.detail: At api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From a manifest. Pick a development workspace (it can't be changed later) and paste a manifest with the app name, the Composio redirect URL and your scopes.

steps.title: Add the redirect URL and scopes
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions → check the redirect URL (HTTPS, no #) and the bot/user scopes from the manifest, e.g. channels:history, chat:write. Leave PKCE and token rotation off unless you need them; PKCE can't be turned off later.

steps.title: Paste the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Basic Information → App Credentials: copy Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio auth config.

steps.title: Connect your workspace and run one tool
steps.detail: Connect through the new auth config, check the consent screen shows your app's name, and run one Slack tool.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution → three checklist items tick themselves once a redirect URL and HTTPS are set; confirm you removed hard-coded tokens → Activate Public Distribution. Any workspace can install it straight away.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace (to lift the history limit)
steps.detail: Once 10 or more workspaces actively use the app, submit it. History, file and admin scopes get an enhanced review; prepare a clear justification for each scope.

blockers.workaround: Grow installs on public distribution first; posting isn't limited meanwhile

steps.title: Marketplace review
steps.detail: Up to 10 business days for preliminary feedback, then up to 10 weeks of functional review.

whileYouWait.text: Keep history-heavy users on Composio managed auth until your listing is approved.
Installs that happened before the limit started aren't throttled.

gotchas.text: New unlisted installs read history at 1 request/minute and 15 messages per call — too slow for summarizing.
Marketplace submission needs 10 active workspaces, so plan for a period on public distribution.
History, file and admin scopes trigger an enhanced Marketplace review.
Switching from managed auth to your own OAuth app doesn't migrate existing connections: users reconnect, or you import their credentials where supported.
Turning on PKCE is permanent for the app.
Slack accepts a sub-path of a registered redirect URL, so register the exact Composio callback and nothing broader.
You can request scopes at runtime that aren't configured on the app, but after a Marketplace listing only approved scopes work.
